entities.name: Gaston III, Count of Foix
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaston III, known throughout Europe as Gaston Phoebus or Fébus, was the formidable eleventh Count of Foix and twenty-fourth Viscount of Béarn, reigning from 1343 until his death in 1391. His lifetime spanned the tumultuous heart of the Hundred Years' War, during which he skillfully navigated the complex political landscape, maintaining a largely independent principality between the competing spheres of influence of the French and English crowns. A figure of immense wealth and military prowess, Phoebus established a court renowned for its luxury and cultural sophistication, making Orthez a significant intellectual and artistic center in late medieval Occitania.

Phoebus's reign was characterized by a shrewd balancing act, avoiding direct allegiance to either France or England while strategically intervening in regional conflicts, notably against the Armagnacs, his traditional rivals. His military campaigns, though often localized, were marked by efficiency and strategic acumen, consolidating his territorial holdings and enhancing the prestige of the House of Foix. Beyond warfare, Gaston was a celebrated patron of the arts and a prolific author, most famously for his 'Livre de Chasse' (Book of the Hunt), a comprehensive treatise on medieval hunting practices, falconry, and associated ethics, which remains a cornerstone of medieval sporting literature. His administrative reforms and financial management further solidified his power, transforming his domains into one of the richest and best-governed territories in southern France.
